items.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: And there were times that I knew that Benny Goodman was playing

ctx.x: How did the jazz creep into your consciousness?
You know I can remember about that age, a little earlier, around that time, I would just go to the radio shows. And there were times that I knew that Benny Goodman was playing

on the radio. And I was simply drawn to that music. And I just — I remember I couldn’t wait for that show to go on and just, instead of “Baby Snookes,” you know those shows in those days were just — before your time — before everybody’s time. And “Fibber McGee and Molly” and those radio shows, I used to listen to the live broadcasts and stuff like that. And that too, I don’t quite understand why you know? Why that happens, and why you are drawn to a particular work or a particular art, except that I just consider…
